rival:vector-solutions.why: Vector is a bundle, so its rivals differ by module: Lexipol on training and policy content, InTime and Pace on scheduling, Benchmark on performance and early intervention. rival:videray-technologies.evidence: No other roster company sells through-object imaging. The nearest names solve different problems: Berkeley Varitronics detects RF from contraband cellphones (a signal, not an image, and only for phones), Bounce Imaging throws a 360 camera into a room to see the space rather than inside a package, and Boston Dynamics Spot is a robot platform a bomb squad carries the imager on - a complement Videray would mount to, not a substitute.
rival:videray-technologies.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:videray-technologies.why: A bomb squad or corrections unit buying a handheld backscatter X-ray imager has no alternative on this roster. Adjacency to contraband detection and bomb squads is not competition; listing Berkeley Varitronics or Bounce Imaging here would be exactly the Robin Radar/Brinc error.

Apex Officer and Kaiden AI attack that same purchase with VR and AI-voice alternatives.

rival:wrap-technologies.ruled_why: Police trial 2026-09-02: read all 132, spot-checked the five from the rail screenshot
rival:wrap-technologies.why: Wrap is close to alone here. Axon is the one real edge: both sell a handheld device an officer deploys at distance to subdue a subject without lethal force, to the same chief and the same equipment line.
